---
title: "El Niño summer tracker 2026/27"
subtitle: "Rain, heat and dams across South Africa's farming regions through a very strong El Niño summer. Updated every Monday."
---

```{r setup}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ggplot2))
for (f in c("R/theme_sain.R", "R/fetch_enso.R", "R/fetch_power.R", "R/fetch_dws.R",
            "R/metrics_el_nino.R", "R/plots_el_nino.R")) source(f)

rows_to_list <- function(df) lapply(split(df, seq_len(nrow(df))), as.list)
s <- jsonlite::fromJSON("data/processed/summary.json")
s$compare <- rows_to_list(s$compare)
s$regions <- rows_to_list(s$regions)

read <- function(f) readr::read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE)
cum     <- read("data/processed/rain_cumulative_regions.csv")
band    <- read("data/processed/rain_normal_band_regions_1991_2020.csv")
sindex  <- read("data/processed/rain_summer_index_all_seasons.csv")
events  <- read("data/processed/el_nino_events.csv")
regions <- read("data/processed/regions.csv")
sites   <- read("data/processed/sites.csv")
dams_file <- "data/processed/dams_summary_latest.csv"
dam_sum <- if (file.exists(dams_file)) read(dams_file) else NULL
archive_file <- "data/archive/dams_weekly.csv"
archive <- if (file.exists(archive_file)) read(archive_file) else NULL
check_file <- "data/processed/region_check_regions.csv"
check <- if (file.exists(check_file)) read(check_file) else NULL

summer <- Filter(function(z) z$season_type == "summer", s$regions)
driest <- summer[[which.min(vapply(summer, function(z) z$rain_pct_of_normal, 0))]]
wc <- Filter(function(z) z$season_type == "winter", s$regions)
```

**Latest data:** rain to `r fmt_date(s$as_of)``r if (!is.null(s$rain_prelim_from) && !is.na(s$rain_prelim_from)) paste0(" (preliminary from ", fmt_date(s$rain_prelim_from), ")") else ""`; temperature to `r fmt_date(s$heat_as_of)`. Season `r s$season` of the October–April summer rainfall season.

```{r wc-rain, results='asis'}
if (length(wc)) {
  w <- wc[[1]]
  wettest <- w$n_seasons - w$rain_rank_driest + 1
  rank_txt <- if (w$rain_rank_driest <= 5) sprintf(": the %s driest of %d winters since 1981", ordinal(w$rain_rank_driest), w$n_seasons) else
    if (wettest <= 5) sprintf(": the %s wettest of %d winters since 1981", ordinal(wettest), w$n_seasons) else ""
  cat(sprintf(paste0("**Western Cape.** Most of its rain falls from April to September, so it is not in the summer ",
                     "rain figures. Its %s winter (%s) brought %s mm, %d%% of normal%s."),
              w$rain_season, w$rain_period, w$rain_mm, w$rain_pct_of_normal, rank_txt))
}
```

## What the data can't tell us

::: {.cant-tell}
- **El Niño raises the odds of a dry, hot summer; it does not guarantee one.** The very strong 1997/98 event brought near-normal rain to much of the summer rainfall region, while 2015/16 brought widespread drought. Both are shown above for that reason.
- **Rainfall is estimated from satellites and rain gauges, not read from every gauge.** CHIRPS blends satellite estimates with station records on a 5 km grid. It is good at comparing this season with its own past, and weaker for exact local totals, especially for single thunderstorms.
- **The latest weeks are preliminary.** Preliminary CHIRPS uses fewer gauges; final values replace them about three weeks after each month ends, so recent figures can change.
- **Heat figures are modelled.** NASA POWER (about 50 km) fills recent weeks with a near-real-time model and replaces them every few months.
- **Each region is an index of 5 to 12 sites, not every farm.** Rain falls patchily in summer, and one storm can make a district wetter than its region.
- **Recent El Niño index values are provisional** and can be revised for up to two months.
- **Dam totals cover only the dams in the DWS weekly report**, weighted by their capacity.
:::

## Regions and method

Sites are grouped into regions whose seasonal rain rises and falls together. Each region's figures are the average of its sites.

```{r region-table}
reg_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(regions)), function(i) {
  r <- regions[i, ]
  data.frame(Region = r$region, Covers = r$covers,
             Season = if (r$season == "winter") "1 Apr to 30 Sep" else "1 Oct to 30 Apr",
             Sites = paste(sites$site[sites$region_id == r$region_id], collapse = ", "))
}))
if (!is.null(check)) {
  reg_tab$`Sites move together (r)` <- check$r_within[match(regions$region_id, check$region_id)]
}
knitr::kable(reg_tab)
```

- **Season:** 1 October to 30 April for the summer-rainfall regions; 1 April to 30 September for the Western Cape. Normal: the 30 seasons starting 1991 to 2020.
- **Rain:** CHIRPS v3 5-day totals (final where available, otherwise preliminary), the mean of a 0.25° window around each of the region's [sites](../../data/processed/sites.csv), summed from the start of the season. Western Cape winter rain uses CHIRPS monthly totals. Until 21 November 2026 the tracker used NASA POWER rain; a check against CHIRPS showed its near-real-time rain missed early-November storms, so we switched.
- **Heat:** daily maximum temperature (T2M_MAX) from NASA POWER.
- **Summer rain index:** each summer region's rain so far as a share of its normal full-season total, averaged with each region counted equally, so the wet east does not swamp the dry west.
- **Hot day:** daily maximum above the site's own 90th percentile for that time of year (1991–2020, ±7-day window). By construction, a normal season has about one hot day in ten. Counted over 1 October to 30 April in every region, including the Western Cape.
- **Ranks** compare the same dates in every season since 1981/82, the start of the NASA POWER record.
- **Do the regions hold together?** For each pair of sites we correlate their seasonal rain totals since 1981 (Spearman's r). Sites should move more with their own region than with any other, and a blind cluster analysis should find the same groups. The check is rerun with every change to the site list (`tests/check_regions.R`).
- **El Niño strength:** NOAA's Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI). An event is five or more overlapping three-month seasons at +0.5 °C or above.
- **Dams:** DWS Weekly State of Reservoirs, % full weighted by full supply capacity.

## Update log

- `r s$as_of`: latest weekly update.
- 21 November 2026: rain now from CHIRPS v3 instead of NASA POWER (see method).
- 21 November 2026: sites grouped into six climate regions (five summer-rainfall, plus the Western Cape); dam capacity totals corrected (DWS "Total" rows were counted as dams; % full figures were not affected).
